identification.summary: Earth Berberoka (also GamblingPuppet) is a Chinese-speaking-linked threat cluster named by Trend Micro researchers Daniel Lunghi and Jaromir Horejsi in 2022. It mainly targets online gambling sites using multiplatform malware (Windows, Linux, macOS) [S1][S2].
identification.firstObserved: Trend Micro published the first public report in April 2022 [S1].
identification.notes: Check Point's 2026 'Gambling Goblin' cluster is linked to Earth Berberoka with medium-to-high confidence by Check Point; treat it as a linked cluster, not a merged one [S4][S5]. Microsoft has no known mapping for this actor in the record. MITRE group ID is not in the record.

attribution.sponsor: Not attributed to a state. Trend Micro describes the malware as historically attributed to Chinese-speaking actors [S1]. Check Point describes Gambling Goblin as Chinese-speaking [S4].
attribution.confidence: Check Point assesses the Gambling Goblin link to Earth Berberoka with medium-to-high confidence [S4][S6].
attribution.basis: Malware lineage and reuse: PlugX, Gh0st RAT and PuppetLoader [S1]; oRAT codebase and operator routes shared with 2022 Earth Berberoka activity [S4].

objectives: Not stated in the sources gathered as a state objective. Trend Micro reports that primary targets are gambling websites in China [S1]. Check Point reports that the linked 2025-2026 cluster hijacks sites to promote gambling and fuel SEO fraud [S4][S5].

sectors: Brazilian government and education sites (Gambling Goblin, linked cluster)
regions: Brazil (Gambling Goblin, linked cluster, since mid-2025) [S4][S6]
targeting.notes: Trend Micro also observed non-gambling victims: one education-related government institution, two IT services companies and one electronics manufacturer [S1]. Regional scope of the 2025-2026 Brazil activity rests on Check Point's linkage, not on Trend Micro [S4].

capabilities.summary: Upgraded older malware (PlugX, Gh0st RAT) plus PuppetLoader, a five-stage loader that hijacks loaded modules and hides payloads in modified BMP image files, one stage using a flawed RC4 implementation [S1][S2]. Tools target Windows, Linux and macOS [S1]. Distribution observed included a fake Adobe Flash Player installer (15 downloads in China, Dec 2020-Apr 2022) and a backdoored chat app called MiMi [S2]. The linked Gambling Goblin cluster installs malicious Apache modules that proxy visitors to phishing pages, and uses Linux tools DownPro, AlphaAgent, oRAT, a 3snake-based credential stealer and an SSH brute-forcer [S4][S6].

campaigns.name: Fake Flash installer and MiMi lures
campaigns.summary: Trend Micro logged 15 downloads of a fake Adobe Flash Player installer in China and describes a backdoored chat app, MiMi, that runs embedded malware in the background [S2].

campaigns.name: Trend Micro disclosure of Earth Berberoka
campaigns.summary: Trend Micro names the group and reports gambling-site targeting with PlugX, Gh0st RAT and PuppetLoader across three platforms [S1].

campaigns.summary: Detailed multiplatform analysis; date inferred from the report URL path [S2].

campaigns.name: Gambling Goblin (linked cluster)
campaigns.summary: Check Point reports compromised Brazilian .gov.br and education sites running malicious Apache modules to redirect to gambling and phishing pages, active since mid-2025; published 2026-09-02 and linked to Earth Berberoka at medium-to-high confidence [S4][S6].

diamond.adversary: Chinese-speaking actor cluster; no state sponsor identified in sources [S1][S4].
diamond.capability: PlugX, Gh0st RAT, PuppetLoader, oRAT, AlphaAgent, malicious Apache modules [S1][S4].
diamond.infrastructure: Compromised legitimate web servers, including Brazilian government sites, and phishing networks in Vietnamese, Spanish and English, with daily-generated domains [S4][S6]. Indicator files for 2022 activity are listed in Trend Micro's record but were not opened.
diamond.victim: Gambling sites and customers, plus a few non-gambling organizations; later Brazilian government and education sites [S1][S4].
diamond.socioPolitical: Not determined. Activity appears financially or SEO-fraud oriented in recent reporting, but this is not settled [S4].
diamond.technology: Windows, Linux and macOS endpoints; Apache web servers [S1][S4].

gaps: Trend Micro's primary report, white paper and IOC files and Check Point's full report could not be fetched; content here relies on search-result summaries and should be re-verified.
The June 2022 Trend follow-up source date was inferred from the URL path.
No state sponsorship, motive, or government attribution is established.
Related-cluster status of Gambling Goblin is vendor-assessed, not confirmed.
Initial access vector for the Brazil activity was reportedly not observed directly by Check Point (secondary, Portuguese-language coverage).
No MITRE group ID or Microsoft actor name is known.

implications.jipoe: Analyst assessment derived from cited sources; validate before use. STEP 1: Internet-facing web servers (Apache) and gambling or casino platforms are the relevant terrain; no military targets appear in the sources. STEP 2: The group reuses mature RATs and builds multiplatform loaders, giving it reach across Windows, Linux and macOS [S1][S4]. STEP 3: Observed pattern is lure or compromised site, then loader, then RAT or Apache module [S2][S4]. STEP 4: MLCOA is continued financially or SEO-motivated compromise of web servers and gambling-related organizations. MDCOA is repurposing hijacked government web infrastructure for broader phishing or malware hosting. Candidate indicators: unexpected Apache modules, BMP files carrying payloads, SSH brute-force against Linux hosts [S4].
implications.jcc2: Analyst assessment derived from cited sources; validate before use. (1) Situational awareness: relevance to DoD missions is low and indirect; track as a commodity-style threat to public web infrastructure. (2) Authorities: any action against compromised foreign government sites belongs to host-nation or law-enforcement channels. (3) Mission assurance: audit Linux web servers for unauthorized Apache modules and credential theft. (4) Coordination: share indicators with partner CERTs; Brazilian government sites were affected [S4].

provenance.importedSummary: According to TrendMicro, Earth Berberoka is a threat group originating from China that mainly focuses on targeting gambling websites. This group's campaign uses multiple malware families that target the Windows, Linux, and macOS platforms that have been attributed to Chinese-speaking actors. Aside from using tried-and-tested malware families that have been upgraded, such as PlugX and Gh0st RAT, Earth Berberoka has also developed a brand-new complex, multistage malware family, which has been dubbed PuppetLoader.
